sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 41
title: Volume of Gold from Mass and Density
statement: Gold is sold by the troy ounce (31.103 g). What is the volume of 1 troy ounce of pure gold?

givenValues.description: Mass of 1 troy ounce of gold

solution.approach: Use the density formula to find volume from mass and density

steps.explanation: Density is given in kg/m³, so we need mass in kg

hints.hint: You need the density of gold and the relationship between density, mass, and volume.
Use ρ = m/V and solve for V. Don't forget to convert grams to kilograms.

problemSpecificErrors.howToDetect: Answer is off by factor of 1000
problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Make sure to convert grams to kilograms to match the density units

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 42
title: Volume of Mercury from Mass and Density
statement: Mercury is commonly supplied in flasks containing 34.5 kg (about 76 lb.). What is the volume in liters of this much mercury?

solution.approach: Use density formula to find volume, then convert to liters

hints.hint: Use the relationship between density, mass, and volume to find the volume in m³.
V = m/ρ, then convert m³ to liters using 1 m³ = 1000 L.

problemSpecificErrors.howToDetect: Answer in m³ instead of L
problemSpecificErrors.feedback: The problem asks for volume in liters. Convert using 1 m³ = 1000 L

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 43
title: Mass of Air in Deep Breath
statement: What is the mass of a deep breath of air having a volume of 2.00 L? Discuss the effect taking such a breath has on your body's volume and density.

givenValues.description: Density of air at sea level

solution.approach: Use density formula to find mass, then discuss physiological effects

steps.explanation: Density is in kg/m³, so volume must be in m³

hints.hint: Use the density of air and the volume to find mass. Remember to convert units properly.
m = ρV, where ρ = 1.29 kg/m³ for air. Convert 2.00 L to m³ first.
Convert: 2.00 L = 0.002 m³, then m = (1.29 kg/m³)(0.002 m³)

problemSpecificErrors.error: Not converting liters to cubic meters
problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Convert liters to m³: 1 L = 0.001 m³

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 44
title: Rock Density from Displacement Method
statement: A straightforward method of finding the density of an object is to measure its mass and then measure its volume by submerging it in a graduated cylinder. What is the density of a 240-g rock that displaces 89.0 cm³ of water?

givenValues.description: Volume of displaced water (= volume of rock)

solution.approach: Use the definition of density with given mass and volume

steps.explanation: Convert mass to kg and volume to m³
steps.equation: m = 240 \text{ g} = 0.240 \text{ kg}, \quad V = 89.0 \text{ cm³} = 89.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m³}

hints.hint: The volume of water displaced equals the volume of the rock. Use the definition of density.
ρ = m/V. Convert grams to kg and cm³ to m³ before calculating.

problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Carefully convert: 1 g = 0.001 kg, 1 cm³ = 10⁻⁶ m³

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 45
title: Coffee Mug Radius from Volume and Depth
statement: Suppose you have a coffee mug with a circular cross-section and vertical sides (uniform radius). What is its inside radius if it holds 375 g of coffee when filled to a depth of 7.50 cm? Assume coffee has the same density as water.

solution.approach: Find volume from mass and density, then use cylindrical volume formula to find radius

steps.description: Convert height to meters and substitute

hints.hint: First find the volume of coffee using its mass and density, then use the volume formula for a cylinder.
V = m/ρ gives the volume, then V = πr²h for a cylinder. Solve for r.
V = 0.375 kg / 1000 kg/m³ = 3.75×10⁻⁴ m³, then r = √(V/πh)

problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Keep all units consistent - use meters throughout or convert at the end

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 50
title: Force on Nail Tip from High Pressure
statement: The tip of a nail exerts tremendous pressure when hit by a hammer because it exerts a large force over a small area. What force must be exerted on a nail with a circular tip of 1.00-mm diameter to create a pressure of 3.00 × 10⁹ N/m²?

solution.approach: Use pressure definition P = F/A to find force, calculating area from diameter

steps.description: Calculate radius and convert to meters
Apply pressure formula to find force

hints.hint: Use P = F/A. You'll need to find the area of the circular nail tip first.
Area = πr², where r = d/2. Convert diameter to meters, then calculate area and use F = PA.
r = 0.5 mm = 5×10⁻⁴ m, A = π(5×10⁻⁴)² m², then F = (3×10⁹ N/m²) × A

problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Remember A = πr², where r = d/2, not A = πd²
Convert mm to m: 1 mm = 0.001 m

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 51
title: Mercury Column Height for 1 atm Pressure
statement: A glass tube contains mercury. What would be the height of the column of mercury which would create pressure equal to 1.00 atm?

solution.approach: Use hydrostatic pressure formula P = ρgh

steps.explanation: Pressure at bottom of fluid column due to fluid weight

hints.hint: The pressure at the bottom of a fluid column is P = ρgh. Solve for h.
Use P = ρgh with P = 1 atm = 101,325 Pa and the density of mercury.

problemSpecificErrors.error: Using wrong value for atmospheric pressure

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 52
title: Ocean Pressure at Mariana Trench Depth
statement: The greatest ocean depths on Earth are found in the Marianas Trench near the Philippines. Calculate the pressure due to the ocean at the bottom of this trench, given its depth is 11.0 km and assuming the density of seawater is constant all the way down.

solution.approach: Use hydrostatic pressure formula P = ρgh for the pressure due to water column

steps.explanation: This gives pressure due to water column only

hints.hint: Use P = ρgh to find the pressure due to the water column. Don't forget atmospheric pressure acts at the surface.
Convert 11.0 km to meters first, then apply P = ρgh with seawater density.
P = (1025 kg/m³)(9.81 m/s²)(11,000 m) - this gives pressure from water only

problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Convert km to m: 11.0 km = 11,000 m
Problem asks for pressure 'due to the ocean' - this means just the water pressure

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 64
title: Fraction of Ice Submerged in Water
statement: What fraction of ice is submerged when it floats in freshwater, given the density of water at 0°C is very close to 1000 kg/m³?

solution.approach: Apply Archimedes' principle: buoyant force equals weight of floating object

steps.explanation: For floating object: weight = buoyant force

steps.description: Simplify and solve for volume ratio

hints.hint: When an object floats, the buoyant force equals its weight. Use Archimedes' principle.
Weight of ice = buoyant force = weight of displaced water. This leads to ρ_ice × V_ice = ρ_water × V_submerged.
Fraction submerged = V_sub/V_total = ρ_ice/ρ_water = 917/1000

problemSpecificErrors.howToDetect: Getting fraction > 1 or using water density in numerator
problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Fraction submerged = ρ_object/ρ_fluid for floating objects

sourceReference: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Chapter 14, Problem 66
title: Rock Properties from Apparent Mass in Water
statement: A rock with a mass of 540 g in air is found to have an apparent mass of 342 g when submerged in water. (a) What mass of water is displaced? (b) What is the volume of the rock? (c) What is its average density? Is this consistent with the value for granite?

solution.approach: Use the difference between actual and apparent mass to find buoyant force, then calculate volume and density

steps.explanation: Buoyant force equals weight of displaced water
Volume of displaced water equals volume of rock

finalAnswer.text: (a) 198 g, (b) 1.98×10⁻⁴ m³, (c) 2730 kg/m³ (consistent with granite ~2700 kg/m³)

hints.hint: The difference between mass in air and apparent mass in water tells you about the buoyant force.
Buoyant force = (mass in air - apparent mass) × g. This equals the weight of displaced water.
Mass of displaced water = 540g - 342g = 198g. This water has volume 198 cm³ = volume of rock.

problemSpecificErrors.error: Confusing apparent mass with actual mass
problemSpecificErrors.howToDetect: Using 342g as the rock's actual mass
problemSpecificErrors.feedback: Apparent mass is what the scale reads underwater. True mass is 540g.

problemSpecificErrors.howToDetect: Not connecting displaced water volume to rock volume
problemSpecificErrors.feedback: The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the submerged object
